title: Kolkata Metro to run longer hours and extra trains on Blue and Green lines for Kali Puja
dek: On Sunday the Blue Line will run 152 services and the Green Line 123, with the last trains at about 11 pm. The Purple and Orange lines will stay shut, as on every Sunday.
author: Declaration Desk
body:
Kolkata Metro will run extra trains and keep two of its lines open later than usual on Sunday, 8 November, for Kali Puja, Metro Railway said in a statement on Friday.

The Blue Line, between Dakshineswar and Shahid Khudiram, will run 152 services, 76 in each direction. Trains will start at about 8 am from both ends, an hour earlier than a normal Sunday, according to reports, and the last train from Shahid Khudiram to Dakshineswar will leave at 11 pm. The last train in the other direction leaves Dakshineswar at 10.40 pm.

The Green Line, between Howrah Maidan and Salt Lake Sector V, will run 123 services instead of the usual 111, with the first trains at 8 am from Howrah Maidan and 8.02 am from Sector V. The last trains will leave both ends at 11 pm, 30 minutes later than usual.

The Yellow Line between Noapara and Jai Hind Bimanbandar (the airport) will run its normal Sunday timetable of 78 services, with the last trains at 9 pm from Noapara and 9.20 pm from the airport. The Purple and Orange lines do not run on Sundays and will stay closed.

Kali Puja and Diwali fall on Sunday this year. The state government has issued crowd-safety rules for Kali Puja pandals after a crush at a Durga Puja pandal in Chorbagan, north Kolkata, killed 19 people last month.
